ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It also names the implementer's report file and the re-review rules.

ACTION: Read `docs/sync.md` around line 12 and grep the file for `dry_run`. This shows the target and any other wrong spelling in the same file before I edit.

ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/re-review-prompt.md`, the template for the scoped re-review.

ACTION: Edit `docs/sync.md`. Change `--dry_run` to `--dry-run` on line 12, and on any other line in this file with the same wrong spelling.

ACTION: Commit the edit. This gives the fix its own commit, so the re-review has a clear diff range.

ACTION: Append a note to the implementer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. It says I changed the flag name in `docs/sync.md`, that the change alters no behavior, and that no test covers it.

ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD` for the fix commit. Use the path it reports.

ACTION: Dispatch the scoped re-review on `sonnet`. The diff is one docs line, so the standard tier fits. The prompt gives the re-review template, F1 quoted from the reviewer, the diff file path, and the plan's global constraints copied verbatim. It asks for ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED on F1 and for any new Critical or Important finding. It does not say how severe F1 is or what to skip.

Message to my partner:

F1 is the reviewer's finding that `docs/sync.md:12` says `--dry_run` while the code, help text and tests say `--dry-run`. It is a wording fix in one file, so I will make it myself and send it to a scoped re-review.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The skill lets the controller fix a wording-only change in one file. A fix subagent would cost more than the edit.
- The fix still gets a re-review. The report file records that no test covers it, because nothing reads `docs/sync.md`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
